title: Dynamic Arrays
summary: How std::vector works inside - a contiguous block with a size and a capacity, growth by doubling and why it gives amortised O(1) push_back, the cost of inserting and erasing in the middle, building a small vector class with a rule-of-five, and what invalidates iterators.

cards.q: A dynamic array grows its capacity by 1.5× when full. What is the amortised cost of push_back?
cards.a:
O(1)

Any constant growth factor above 1 keeps the total copying proportional to n.

cards.q: Why does erasing the first element of a std::vector take O(n)?
cards.a:
Every other element shifts one place to the left

The elements must stay contiguous, so they all move down by one.

cards.q: You hold a reference to v[2] and then call v.push_back(x). Is the reference still safe to use?
cards.a:
Only if the push did not reallocate

Reallocation moves the elements to a new block, leaving old references dangling. If capacity was reserved first, no reallocation happens.
